A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Model-Preserving Adaptive Rounding and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantization experiments on Llama and Gemma models, Hessian analyses, and appendix comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen 3 8B evaluations and a calibration-sequence sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The Kronecker-factored rounding procedure, Hessian Sketches A and B, and their initializations are retained. The iterative rounding and backward-pass code in A.6, A.8, and A.9 is unchanged apart from formatting.

E1.justification: The new Qwen evaluation adds MMLU knowledge questions and GSM8K mathematical reasoning, extending task coverage beyond the earlier benchmarks. Existing calibration data and evaluation datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–7 retain LDLQ, GuidedQuant, DiscQuant, Google’s Gemma QAT, and CBQ in their respective comparisons. New Qwen experiments reuse LDLQ; the additional methods discussed in Section 4 are not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Qwen 3 8B, 4K-context Wikitext2 evaluation, zero-shot MMLU, four-shot chain-of-thought GSM8K with exact match, and a 2K–64K calibration-sequence sweep. Existing experiment settings are retained. A.1’s blanket 8192-token statement is not reconciled with the new tables’ 4K labels.

E4.justification: v2 already examines sequence count versus Hessian cosine similarity in Figure 3. v3 adds A.11 and Table 9, testing how 2K–64K calibration sequences affect quantized-model quality and GPU-hour cost. Existing incoherence-processing and finetuning analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new sequence counts measure calibration sample size, not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain identical data. New Tables 8–9 report Qwen results: at 2 bits, YAQA-B has KL 0.205 versus LDLQ’s 0.285; using only 2K calibration sequences gives KL 0.227. Improvements are not universal: 4-bit MMLU is 72.78 for YAQA-B versus 73.04 for LDLQ.

T1.justification: The structural-nilpotence definitions and lemmas, error-bound theorems, Hessian-sketch derivations, and A.7 proofs are mathematically retained. Changes concern numbering, notation layout, and equivalent wording.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that YAQA generalizes LDLQ, provides the first end-to-end quantization error bounds, reduces KL by approximately 30%, achieves lower KL than QAT, and adds no inference overhead. v3’s explicit KL and weight-only LLM wording clarifies the existing contribution.

C2.justification: v3 connects roughly doubled rounding time relative to LDLQ with the structural-nilpotence prediction. It also interprets the new sequence sweep as demonstrating strong quality at much lower calibration cost. Existing interpretations of sketch bias, KL preservation, and finetuning remain.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future code release; v3 supplies a repository link in A.1. Table 9 adds calibration counts and GPU-hour costs, including 1 GPU-hour for 2K sequences and 30 for 64K. Existing implementation details and code listings are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including QuaRot, SpinQuant, NestQuant, SmoothQuant, LSQ, LLM-QAT, low-rank QAT, and Large Lookup Layers. Section 4 expands the rationale for selecting LDLQ-based comparisons and omitting other PTQ and older QAT methods, without replacing the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose edits, clarifies KL terminology, expands baseline-selection discussion, and makes First Order Quantization Methods a peer subsection. It also adds A.11 and acknowledgements and renames the ethics statement. The overall argument and section order remain.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column ICML main-text layout with new title, affiliation, and running-header formatting, and reflows the appendices. Figure 2’s panels change from horizontal to vertical arrangement, existing displays are resized or relocated, and Tables 8–9 are added. The original plotted content is retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–9 add useful knowledge and mathematical-reasoning evaluations and quantify calibration cost versus quality, while A.1 supplies code-access information absent from v2. These incrementally strengthen empirical support and reproducibility without changing the established method, proofs, or results. A limited documentation drawback is the unreconciled 8192-token statement in A.1 versus the new tables’ 4K evaluation labels.
